_description: Golden reference: per-scene entity extraction for The Mariner screenplay, source-first verified against every action line. Used to validate scene_breakdown_v1 action-line entity extraction.
_notes: characters_in_action: characters introduced or mentioned in action/description lines (the target of LLM extraction)
characters_in_dialogue: characters appearing as dialogue cues (found by structural parser, included for union)
props: narratively significant objects characters interact with as tools/weapons/MacGuffins — NOT costume/wardrobe, set dressing, or incidentals
YOUNG MARINER never speaks; THUG 1 and THUG 3 never receive their own numbered dialogue cues, while the later generic THUG cue cannot be assigned to a specific thug
Scene numbering follows all 15 semantic INT./EXT. headings; inline BEGIN FLASHBACK headings are boundaries even though the current SCENE_HEADING_RE does not detect that prefix
The summary fields named characters_*_by_current_regex retain their legacy schema names but describe the removed pre-Story-080 action-line regex baseline
summary.unique_characters canonicalizes MARINER to THE MARINER and excludes the unidentified generic THUG dialogue cue

scenes.heading: EXT. CITY CENTRE - NIGHT
scenes.notes: Establishing shot. No named entities. Generic 'homeless' and 'vigilantes' are not characters.

scenes.heading: EXT. RUDDY & GREENE BUILDING - FRONT - NIGHT
scenes.notes: Building exterior description. SUVs are set dressing.

scenes.heading: EXT. RUDDY & GREENE BUILDING - REAR - NIGHT
scenes.notes: THE MARINER first introduction (ALL CAPS in action). Most action described through sounds (O.S.). Van is a vehicle/set piece, not a hand prop.

scenes.heading: INT. RUDDY & GREEN BUILDING - ELEVATOR
scenes.notes: ROSE first visual introduction (line 42); Mariner is explicitly named in action at lines 49, 65, 96, 98, 122, and 133. Three THUGS introduced line 98. THUG 1 and THUG 3 never receive their own numbered dialogue cues. Line 110 dialogue cue 'THUG' is an unidentified thug speaking through the closed doors. Mariner's costume (SWEATER, BRACERS, TATTOO, BANDOLIER, FISH HOOKS, BOOTS, CAPE, FISHING NET, WEIGHTS) is wardrobe, not props. OAR is the primary weapon. GUNS are wielded by Thugs 1, 2, and 3.

scenes.heading: INT. 11TH FLOOR - CONTINUOUS
scenes.notes: This logical present-day scene envelopes the nested scene 6 flashback, then resumes at line 158. Mariner is explicitly named in action at line 145 and Rose at line 158. FILING CABINET is set dressing. Mariner looks at his TATTOO but it is wardrobe, not a prop.

scenes.heading: BEGIN FLASHBACK: EXT. COASTLINE - DAY - PAST
scenes.notes: BEGIN FLASHBACK scene. 'Young Mariner (8)' is title case, not ALL CAPS. 'his dad (30s, fisherman)' is lowercase description. Both are characters the LLM must identify from context. YOUNG MARINER never speaks in the entire screenplay.

scenes.heading: INT. STAIRWELL - CONTINUOUS
scenes.notes: Most action uses pronouns, but Mariner is explicitly named in action at line 170.

scenes.heading: INT. 12TH FLOOR STAIRWELL - CONTINUOUS
scenes.notes: ROSCO is introduced as 'A thug (ROSCO)' at line 177; Rose and Mariner are also explicitly named throughout the action. GUN is Rosco's dropped weapon that Rose picks up.

scenes.heading: INT. 13TH FLOOR
scenes.notes: VINNIE, MIKEY, and CARLOS are introduced together at line 216; Rose and Mariner are explicitly named in later action. The thugs ready and raise GUNS at lines 235 and 243. FLARE GUN is described as 'a fat, bright-orange pistol' at line 256. OAR is referred to as 'BLOODY OAR' at line 265. 'BOSUN' carved into the oar is a description of the OAR, not a separate prop. Line 256 has the typo 'Mainer' for Mariner.

scenes.heading: INT. 15TH FLOOR
scenes.notes: This logical present-day scene envelopes the nested scene 11 flashback, then resumes at line 309. Mariner and Rose are explicitly named in action before and after it; SALVATORI is introduced at line 352. 'Two THUGS' at line 350 are unnamed extras, not distinct characters, and their raised GUNS support GUN here. PURSE is the MacGuffin containing the blockchain password. OAR is used to break open the door. SUBMACHINE GUN is Salvatori's weapon. Room furnishings (DESK, RUG, BOOKSHELVES, BOOZE, PAINTINGS, MINTS, TUMBLER, CIGAR) are set dressing.

scenes.heading: BEGIN FLASHBACK: EXT. BACKYARD - DAY - PAST
scenes.notes: BEGIN FLASHBACK. Idealized memory version. 'Young Mariner's dad' appears in action text. Weightlifting is described, but no discrete exercise prop is explicitly named; 'bench press' is used as a verb.

scenes.heading: EXT. BACKYARD - DAY - (FLASHBACK)
scenes.notes: Dark/true version of the backyard flashback. Dad PUNCHES Young Mariner. BENCH PRESS is an explicitly named apparatus that Young Mariner actively loads at line 371. The loose weights are components of that interaction rather than a separate prop; discarded bottles are set dressing, and the kicked bottle is incidental.

scenes.heading: INT. STAIRWELL - (BACK TO PRESENT)
scenes.notes: Back to present. All dialogue, no action-line entities.

scenes.heading: EXT. COASTLINE - DAY - (FLASHBACK)
scenes.notes: Dark/true version of the coastline flashback. Dad is drunk and neglectful. Beer bottles are incidental.

scenes.heading: EXT. BACKYARD - DAY - (FLASHBACK)
scenes.notes: Intercut climax. Dialogue is Salvatori/Mariner/Rose in the present overlaid on a flashback scene heading. Mariner, Salvatori, and Rose are all explicitly named in action. 'The thugs take Mariner's OAR' at line 401. Salvatori fires and later points GUN at Rose at lines 403 and 426.

summary.regex_baseline_context: The removed pre-Story-080 runtime action-line path returned ROSE, VINNIE, MIKEY, and SALVATORI on this source. THE MARINER matched the raw regex but was rejected because THE was a character stopword; SALVATORI was returned only because the curly-apostrophe SALVATORI (CONT’D) dialogue cue was misclassified as action. The two lists preserve that actual legacy runtime result, not current behavior.
prop_classification_rules: Props are objects characters physically interact with as tools, weapons, or MacGuffins
Costume/wardrobe (SWEATER, BRACERS, CAPE, etc.) is NOT a prop — separate future story
Set dressing (DESK, RUG, BOOKSHELVES, etc.) is NOT a prop
Incidentals (BOTTLE, BUTTON, DOOR) are NOT props
Descriptive text about a prop (BOSUN carved into OAR) is part of the prop, not a separate entity
